data.headline: Walmart’s global online sales grow 17% as Nasdaq futures funds hold net longs
data.summary: Walmart, a Nasdaq-100 constituent, reported 17% growth in global e-commerce sales and 23% growth in U.S. e-commerce. The two figures cover different markets and give a consumer-side reading alongside the index’s technology earnings.

bull.text: Walmart reported 25% growth in its global advertising business and a 17% rise in membership-fee revenue. How it records advertising depends on the arrangement.

bear.text: The retailer identified a shift in the timing of Flipkart’s Big Billion Days event that affected year-over-year comparisons.

watch.text: In the November 10 E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures report, leveraged funds held a net long of 13,967 contracts, up from 10,073 on November 3. Those positions were measured before Walmart’s release.

limitations: Company sales growth and futures balances measure different exposures. QQQ’s session return, options skew and a comparable analyst consensus remain unverified at publication.

sources.title: SEC EDGAR · Walmart’s November 19 results filing
